text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Swedish state-owned power producer Vattenfall renewed its 903 million markka bid for Finnish regional power company Savon Voima and Finnish Espoon Sahko has also been interest in buying the group.
- State employment authorities' have restored companies' confidence and vacancies and recruiment offered trough state employment offices has increased.
- Next year's state budget to allocate funds to labour ministry for hundreds of new jobs at the employment offices, and government also agreed on support for employers hiring long-term unemployed.
- Finnish farming inspection has been inadequate and more inspectors should be hired, European Commission says and may cut subsidies otherwise, official says.
- Municipalities to lose 800 million markka of corporate tax revenue to state coffers next year, government agrees, replacing an earlier plan to cut state grants.
- Three out of four Chemical workers prefer tax reliefs to nominal pay rises, union poll shows.

- The price of membership certificates in cooperative Helsinki telephone operator Helsingin Puhelin's owner HPY has jumped to 5,000 markka from 3,000 markka this year ahead of the planned share issue and listing this autumn, broker says.
- Forestry group UPM-Kymmene seeks a major acquisition in magazine papers in the U.S., CEO Juha Niemela says.
- State budget cuts in construction will hit firms hard and overturn thousands of contracts, industry says.
- The state budget for 1998 will be the last made in markka only if the thrid phase of EMU takes place at the beginnig of 1999, and the 1999 will already include euro elements.
- Engineering group JOT studies stock exhange listing in Helsinki and on Nasdaq in the U.S., and production possibilities in North-America.

- The state deficit or stringent income taxes are not Finland's main problem; the government's failure to reach a track of halved unemployement is, says opposition leader, Centre Party chairman Esko Aho.
- State plans to cut funds from municipalities in next year's budget is a strong offence against their self-government, local government lobby says.
